newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shekel gains against dollar, basket.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shekel gains against dollar, basket.

text.p: The Israeli shekel rose against the dollar and a basket of key foreign currencies on Tuesday as the business sector converted foreign currency for monthend payments, dealers said.

"The shekel continues to rise but volume is relatively low. The main reason for today's gain was that the business sector converted foreign currency into shekels for end-of-the-month payments," said a dealer at the First International Bank of Israel.

The representative rate for the dollar was fixed at 3.5340 shekels compared with 3.5450 on Monday. The basket, composed of the dollar, mark, sterling, French franc and yen, was fixed at 3.7782 against 3.7886 on Monday.
On the crosses, the shekel traded at 3.0109 shekels per 100 yen compared with 3.0259 on Monday, and against the mark at 1.9269 shekels compared with 1.9203 on Monday.
In late afternoon, the dollar was trading at 3.5350 shekels.
- Dan Gerstenfeld, Tel Aviv newsroom, 972-3-537-2211 x233
